body:
Mignarda (mignarda@aol.com) wrote:

: By "delusions" I'm certain the "professionals" are referencing Ted's
: beliefs regarding the technological society. In that case it would
: be sufficient, for the purpose of proving paranoia, that a person be
: merely mistaken in his prognoses.

I thought it's clear from the clinical definition of paranoid
schizophrenia that the delusions have to be a bit more intricate than
this, and usually combined with some other affective symptoms... such
as seeking social isolation, his depression, and his sexual issues.

We'll hopefully understand more if we ever see the Johnson report.

from my last msg -- the PS definition:
"The individual may see himself or herself as the pivot of all that
happens.
...
Perplexity is also common early on and frequently leads to a
belief that everyday situations possess a special, usually
sinister, meaning intended uniquely for the individual.
...
Examples of the most common paranoid symptoms are:

(a) delusions of persecution, reference, exalted birth, special
mission, bodily change, or jealousy;"

Of course, I think it's clearly shown that paranoid schizophrenia
is a sympton of our modern world.  Socio-biologists (evolutionary
psychologists) call this mismatch theory.  Human minds weren't
designed when airplanes and skyscrapers walked the earth.

   "[I] attribute the social and psychological problems of modern society
   to the fact that society requires people to live under conditions
   radically different from those under which the human race evolved ..."
   -- FC
   
There's a link to the "Evolution of Despair" Robert Wright article
here:
http://www.cs.umass.edu/~ehaugsja/unabom/analysis.html
   
E
